# The concept drawings at a glance {#sec-appendix-drawings}

The four concept drawings (@sec-live-drawings) are developed and in use. Each is hand-drawn in Excalidraw and revealed stage by stage on the slides as the summary of its block. This appendix is the at-a-glance index; the design brief for each lives in @sec-live-drawings.

| # | Drawing | Makes clear | When in the session | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Local and remote (@sec-drawing-local-remote) | Two copies of the work, and Git moving changes between them | Summary of "create and clone" | Done |
| 2 | The commit cycle (@sec-drawing-commit-cycle) | Stage, commit, push; a commit as a labeled snapshot | Summary of "the commit cycle" | Done |
| 3 | Branching (@sec-drawing-branching) | A branch as a parallel line of work that splits and rejoins | Summary of "work on a branch", merge point left open | Done |
| 4 | The pull request (@sec-drawing-pull-request) | A merge with a human review step in the middle | Summary of "pull request, review, merge", completing Drawing 3 | Done |

## How to use this list

- To change a drawing, edit its `.excalidraw` source and re-render the frame sequence following `README-drawings.md` next to the images (in the cohort and template repositories), then update the design brief in @sec-live-drawings if the story changed.
- If you add a new drawing, add a row here and a section there, keeping the numbering in sync with the run of show (@sec-run-of-show).
- Keep the "When in the session" column aligned with the run of show so the drawings stay tied to the moment they support.
